incident_description:
On 11 April 2011, an aerosol can of Oneida Silver Polish Spray literally exploded inside a cabinet in our laundry room.  The exploding can blew the cabinets doors open and sprayed its toxic 1,1,1 - Trichloroethane contents in every direction.  The can exploded with such force that it crushed an adjacent can of Brasso like it was a beer can.  Had anyone been in the laundry room at the time, there is absolutely no question serious injury would have occurred. Damage was limited to permanent stains on cabinet doors, appliances, walls, and some clothing. Cleanup of that mess, to the extent possible, was also undoubtedly a somewhat hazardous undertaking.
	This product is, or was, manufactured in the U.S. by Connoisseurs Products Corp. of Woburn, MA.  They brand the product using the trademarked Oneida name under a license from Oneida, Ltd. in Oneida, NY.  The can in question was admittedly old, perhaps 5 years or older, and the product appears to no longer be marketed by Connoisseurs.  Nonetheless, post-explosion examination of the remains of the can revealed no obvious corrosion of any of its seams (it appeared to rupture along its vertical seam).  At no time in its life was it ever exposed to heat or stored in any dangerous environment, e.g.,  above 120-degrees F (as the warning on the can states).
	I have twice attempted to contact Connoisseurs via email simply to tell them of my experience with their product and to alert them to the possibility that thousands? tens-of-thousands? of such cans are likely still being used around the country---cans that are in essence ticking time bombs.   Connoisseurs has never even acknowledged those contacts.
justification: The incident caused significant damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an event is considered rare given the specific conditions described.

incident_description: After seeing someone post photos online of a positive lead test on the water bottle my son uses in his lunchbox, I decided to contact the company to inquire.  They insisted their products are lead-free.  However, on one of the styles they carry--the one my son was using--there is exposed lead solder on the bottom of the bottle.  I bought an EPA approved test kit and tested it myself.  Sure enough, it tests positive for "hazardous levels of lead" (according to the test kit; the test stick turned very dark pink immediately upon contact).  The company's water bottles are primarily made of stainless steel, but they are vacuum sealed for insulation.  There is, therefore, a hole at the bottom where they suck out the air, and it is sealed up with solder.  The size of the hole is not tiny; it is approximately 1/2 inch in diameter.  Most of their water bottles are coated in a spray painted color, so in that case the paint covers up the solder so it is not exposed.  However, they also offer the option of an "all stainless steel" bottle with no paint.  This is the one I chose, thinking it would have the lowest chance of anything toxic.  On these bottles, there is nothing at all covering the lead on the bottom.  Other companies (such as [REDACTED]) put an additional steel cap on the bottom, which covers up the solder.  Hydro Flask does not.  They are one of the few companies to make a small sized insulated bottle, which makes it the perfect size to put in lunch boxes, and which makes it very popular for children.  That means that lots of little children's hands are touching the lead, and inevitably, children's hands end up in their mouths.  I contacted the company with this information, and they admitted it is lead solder.  But then they said they sent their products out to a CPSC approved testing lab who said all of their products are within safe limits for lead.  Overall, I could see this is true.  However, having a dime-sized spot of pure lead on the bottom of a water bottle that children use is unbelievably unsafe, so I can't imagine any lab would call that safe.  The company says they are going to switch to lead-free solder, but that still means all of the consumers who already have the bottles in their children's hands will never know it, and the stores currently stocking them will continue to have them available.  This is scary!
justification: Exposed lead solder on children's water bottles poses a significant health risk, with potential for lead exposure and poisoning.

incident_description:
I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the sale of non-breathable Polyvinyl Chloride dog crate covers sold on Amazon by several Chinese companies making false claims that their crate covers are breathable. My company, [REDACTED], has been making crate covers since 1999.
After reading horrific reviews on the lack of breathability resulting in overheated dogs and numerous adults complaining of toxic smells causing headaches, my company purchased dog crate covers on Amazon from 3 different Chinese companies. After much research, it was determined that the ASTM D-737 would be the best test to measure the Air Flow and Breathability of these crate covers. 
[REDACTED] hired an accredited lab ISO 17025 to test our dog crate cover and 3 Chinese crate covers that are coated with PVC. The ASTM D-737 test results show the Chinese crate covers had zero air permeability. 
I urge you to take immediate action to ban PVC Coated dog crate covers due to the following Health Risks: 

1.	PVC Coated Material is not breathable and does not provide the proper amount of oxygen for our dogs basic needs. When material is coated in PVC, no oxygen can pass through. Everyday thousands of dogs are kept in pvc covered crates forced to breathe toxic chemicals in a low oxygen environment.  Not only are non-breathable crate covers extremely dangerous for dogs but families with small children are the largest demographic of dog owners therefore if adults are getting headaches from the toxic smells of the pvc imagine what these chemicals are doing to the children and pets in the homes. Please read the attached reviews, many dog owners mention their dog crying in the crate due to the lack of breathability, dogs panting and wet bedding from overheating, several mention condensation and mildew on the inside of the crate covers and even dogs getting skin irritations.

2.	Polyvinyl chloride, or PVC, is a major source of phthalates that are known endocrine disruptors that can cause skin irritation and cancer. They were banned from children's toys and should be banned from pet bedding and pet toys. Children and pets are particularly vulnerable to the effects of phthalates because of their body weight. Much like humans, our pet's skin is permeable and will absorb harmful chemicals it comes into contact with. PVC is carcinogenic if inhaled or eaten. Dog crates are used to train puppies and contain older dogs. Crate Covers are part of the crate bedding and provides den like privacy. However, dogs should not be enclosed with these PVC coated covers and forced to breathe toxic chemicals in a low oxygen environment. Puppies and young dogs are teething when they are crate training, chewing on material is common. It is not safe to ingest pvc coated materials and when they lick their paws and their body, the chemicals are absorbed faster. According to The Veterinary Cancer Society, cancer is the leading cause of death in 47% of dogs. 


3.	Chinese sellers on Amazon claim that their dog crate covers are Well Ventilated, breathable, Made of harmless high-quality materials to bring comfort and safety to pets, The ventilation design not only provides private space for your dogs, but also prevents them felling anxious from stuffiness, provides good breathability are all examples of their false claims.  The certified test results on all 3 Chinese crate covers showed 0 air permeability. 

4.	Labeling- None of the 3 Chinese crate covers had a fabric content label which should be a violation of The Fair Packaging and Labeling Act. It is obvious that these crate covers are all coated with pvc however only 1 of 3 covers had a CA Prop 65 chemical warning label affixed to the product. One of the Chinese companies, [REDACTED]  had no labels not even a Country-of-Origin label or Manufacturer name and place of business affixed in a permanent fashion as required by US Customs. Amazon should share in the responsibility of labeling just as most large retailers do. 
Just like children, pets are extremely vulnerable and must be protected. Phthalates in pet products including beds, crate covers, and toys should be banned for the health and safety of our furry children that have no voice. 
[REDACTED] has been designing pet bedding since 1999. All our products are made with pet-friendly materials. Our factory is certified by OEKO-TEX Standard 100. Our products were tested and passed CA Prop 65 test and CPSC Lead and Cadmium. We prioritize the health and well-being of our pets over profitability.  

I hope you will take immediate action to ban the sale of PVC dog crate covers on Amazon and PVC in all dog products.
justification: The incident describes potential health risks to dogs including overheating, toxic chemical exposure, and possible long-term effects like cancer, indicating injury or death.

incident_description:
My 91 yo mother was given 2 boxes of Garlic Parsley potatoes by a family member. On August
6, 2018, she placed one tray of potatoes in her microwave per package directions, setting timer
for 5 minutes. 17 seconds before the 5 minutes was up she smelled something burning and saw
black smoke coming from the microwave. She opened the microwave and the tray caught on
fire. She used a dishtowel to attempt to put out the fire and remove the tray from the
microwave. The melted plastic and charred potatoes fell from the bottom of the tray onto her
floor, causing two burn spots in her vinyl floor The black plastic also melted onto her turntable.
I entered her home the next day and immediately smelled smoke. On examining the tray that
contained the potatoes, I noticed an approx 4 inch circle melted in the bottom of the tray. The
potatoes were charred and the burnt smell was horrific  it lingered in her kitchen for several
days even after washing down the inside of the microwave and the upper and lower cabinets.
Luckily her clothing did not catch on fire and she was not injured, just visibly shaken & upset. I
took the second carton of Garlic Potatoes to my own home to determine if my Mom had done
something wrong or if the problem might have been with her microwave. Following package
directions to the letter, the tray was placed in the microwave, setting the timer for 5 minutes;
after I minutes 30 seconds, the tray began to smoke. The smell was nauseating. A small hole
had started to melt in the bottom of the tray and there was a scorch mark on the turntable. I
emailed a complaint to the customer service address and received a response from [REDACTED]. After answering all her questions, sending pictures, bar
code and "Enjoy by" date info which was December 19, 2017, I received her final answer: "As
this product is past the Enjoy Date of December 19, 2017, it would have to be packed on
October 28, 2017. Product is approx 10 months old, most probably as potatoes continue to lose
moisture over time and become dry, and may have contributed to catching fire. Be assured our
current product in the market is fully tested." She offered to send coupons for free products. She
overlooked the fact that the package gave an "Enjoy by" date but not a warning that the package
would melt and burn if used past this date. Also, the "Enjoy by" date is barely visible, in yellow
print on the side of the black tray, not on the cardboard carton. I understand that the product
may lose some nutritional value if used beyond a certain date, but this is a safety hazard. I feel
my mother is entitled to compensation to cover damage to her vinyl floor and a new microwave
which may now be compromised by the fire. There may be other cartons of Little Potatoes that
are past the "Enjoy by" date, exposing people like my mother to injury or property damage.
justification: The incident involved a fire and property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
I purchased the 2-pack  Blue Whale Muriatic Acid  (2x1gallon jugs).  I placed the box in my back seat.  The box dimensions are rectangular (not square), so easy to tip. I did not notice that the box had fallen over on its side as I drove.  The acid burned through the cap on one of the jugs and proceeded to spill out onto my back seat and floor.  My skin began itching and I started to feel the burn in my lungs before I was able to pull over. The corners and side of the white box were black and corroded. As I pulled the box out,  it fell apart and the acid splashed on my hands and arm.   There was no way to transport or safely close and dispose of the acid.  I found a drain to dump the remaining acid, afraid to just throw it in a dumpster where it could harm others. I let the car air out dumping water on the seat and floor. I called the store and they said they were aware the acid could burn through the cap and I should have just taken care and kept the box upright per the warning printed on the box.  My question: If the acid doesn't burn through the plastic used to make the jug, why don't they just make the cap out of that same plastic material?  I used to be able to buy the 4-pack box of acid from the former store (before being bought out by Leslie's) which did not tip easily.  The rectangular 2-pack box is prone to tipping. 
 Customers are just lay-people without protected ways to transport or store these products, so the company should be more responsible in making a container that can hold it safely until use. The warning label doesn't say the acid will burn through the cap.
justification: The acid spill caused skin and lung irritation, indicating injury, and the incident is likely to recur due to the unstable packaging design.

incident_description: While attempting to open a glass jar, it broke in my hand. A large fragment remained in the lid. Idid not notice any indication of damage to the jar prior to it breaking.  The incident required medical attention - I received two stitches and minor adipose tissue removal.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring medical attention (stitches and minor tissue removal), but no death or severe harm occurred.

incident_description: A piece of tin foil was removed from the roll, when wrapping it around the container the tin foil cut my pinky fairly deep. Following week same thing happened to my mother in law on her pointer finger, that's when I realized the product was in fact dangerous.

incident_description: I purchased Holiday Time 20 oz glass reindeer can glass with straw and lid from Walmart in December  of 2023 at an after Christmas sale.  The directions on the label said "hand wash only." When I was washing the inside of the glass, it broke and lacerated my hand.  I went to the Emergency Room and received stitches.
justification: The glass broke during hand washing, causing a laceration that required stitches, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My sister me a Make it Mine. I wasnt aware of what it was when I opened it. I opened the envelope and there was a pull tab so I pulled it. Out shot two cardboard boxes that popped out because there were thick elastics inside that had tension on them. When I pulled the tab it released the tension and they shot out. When they shot out they hit me in the hit. I still have a bruise on my eye and it hurt and had blurry vision for a few days.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruise and temporary blurry vision, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while opening the baby food jar it shattered, the piece of the glass that broke off caused lacerations to her right index finger.  She went to the [REDACTED] emergency room in Longview WA where she received stitches and was released for follow up with her physician.
Caller stated that the manufacturer was not contacted as yet, she stated that she is still enduring pain and difficulty using her hand.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description: (01/24/2024) The consumer stated that the varnish on the box was still tacky when she received the product. Also, the smell was very strong. The varnish got on her hands and on her food. The consumer is not sure if she washed her hands before eating but she started to get headaches and had severe vomiting and diarrhea. The consumer had to go to ER twice.
justification: The consumer experienced severe vomiting, diarrhea, and required ER visits due to exposure to tacky varnish, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents can occur with improper product handling or defects.

incident_description: On February 20th I microwaved a Healthy Choice Cafe Steamer for the time recommended on the package.  When it was done I removed it from the microwave and as I carried it over to remove the insert or tray it touched the inside of my arm by my wrist causing a 2nd degree burn.  This happened in a matter of seconds.  It is painful and took several weeks to heal. This product should never get so hot that it causes permanent scaring as it did to me.
justification: The incident resulted in a 2nd degree burn that took weeks to heal, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as burns from hot food are a known risk but not extremely frequent.

incident_description:
We purchased a Snapware Pyrex Glass Food Storage Set a few years ago. After a couple of years, we noticed the glass containers were being chipped by the snap on the lid. We exchanged them for another set thinking that this had to be a fluke.
A year or so later, we noticed the same problem and began setting aside the damaged containers to take back. This morning, the light reflected off of something in the food we were dishing up from one of the snapware containers. I reached in to remove the debris and discovered it was a shard of glass! We searched through the food for more and found others. One was over an inch long! The container has a huge chip broken off the outside of the rim where the lid snaps on.
justification: Glass shards in food pose a risk of injury if ingested, and the issue has recurred multiple times.

incident_description:
The consumer removed the soda from the 12 pack box it came in.  She was placing it in a cooler, filled with ice, when the can exploded.  

Soda flew into the consumers eyes and she felt a burning sensation.  She rinsed her eyes with water.  However, she had to take an anxiety pill, because of the incident.  No further Rx was needed.

There were not problems with the other cans.


On the date of the incident, it was humid outdoors, but the consumer is not sure what the temperature may have been.

She contact the manufacturer/brand name company and report this to them.
justification: The consumer experienced a burning sensation in her eyes and required an anxiety pill, indicating minor injury.

incident_description:
Over the past two days, I experienced two separate incidents involving glass shards in food stored in Berkley Jensen glass containers. On April 22, I bit into something hard while eating food that had been stored in the [REDACTED], and suspected it might have been a bone or similar. I discarded the food out of caution.

On April 23, while eating a completely different batch of food from a different container in the same set, a glass shard became lodged vertically between my tongue and the roof of my mouth, causing bleeding and immediate pain. I had to remove the glass while driving and swallowed blood.

After inspecting the containers, I found multiple chips around the rims that appear to have come from normal stacking/storage. The product was not dropped or misused. I have photos of the chipped dish, the glass shard, the injury, and the meal. I have also notified my physician and documented the injury in my medical records. This product is dangerous and needs to be investigated.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bleeding and pain) from glass shards in food, and occurred twice in two days with the same product.

incident_description:
On 4/9/10 the consumer's daughter swallowed the white circular paper material inside a Mr. Bubble Bath bottle cap. While the consumer's wife was bathing her daughter she saw her daughter swallow it. The consumer took his daughter to King's Daughters Hospital emergency room located 823 Grand Ave Yazoo City, MS 39194. The doctor examined the child and advised the consumer that the white circular paper material inside the bottle cap that his daughter swallowed would pass threw. The consumer's daughter went home the same day. 

The consumer states during the next 2 years he noticed that his daughter experienced shortness of breathe and would regurgitate her food on several different occasions. 

In 2012 the consumer took his daughter to Blair E. Batson Children's Hospital in Jackson MS and a doctor conducted a Barium test. The doctor advised the consumer that something obstructed his daughter's esophagus and made a pouch. The consumer's daughter had surgery to remove the white circular paper material that she swallowed. The consumer's daughter stayed a few days in the hospital. The consumer's daughter has gone for a yearly examination since her surgery as directed by the doctor. 

The consumer states that the white circular paper material found inside a bottle cap poses a safety hazard due to it not being detected in an X-ray. 

The consumer states this piece of white circular paper material inside a bottle cap is found in many different bottled containers. 

The consumer has not contacted the manufacturer and does not plan to. He does not have the bottle of Mr. Bubble Bath but has the white circular paper material that was inside the bottle cap which his daughter swallowed.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring surgery and ongoing medical examinations, but no death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the description of similar materials in other containers.

incident_description: Today for the SECOND time a chard of glass broke off a jar of Smuckers Sweet Orange Marmalade. I was simply holding the jar and using a knife to scoop out the marmalade from the jar and a chard of glass (about 3/8 ") broke off from the bottom edge of the jar, pierced my skin and cut my finger.  On December 4th of 2021 a chard of glass (about 1/2") from a different jar broke off and landed on the plate of food beneath where I was scooping out the marmalade with a knife. The first time it happened I assumed I must have accidently bumped the marmalade jar on another glass jar in the refrigerator door even though I did not have a memory of doing so. I have been extremely careful since then and this new jar has not been bumped against anything and broke from normal use. I still have the jar from December and I kept the one from today also. If you want to examine or test them please tell me where to send them to you.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut finger) and has occurred twice under similar conditions, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: Ritual does not have child resistant cap on their product which resulted in my child eating half the bottle and having to go to the hospital.
justification: The child ingested half the bottle and required hospitalization, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a bottle of Garden of Life Dr. Formulated Kids Elderberry Immune Gummies for my children. On the evening of September 6, 2025, my five- and four-year-old daughters were able to access the bottle and consume twenty-five gummies. The cap was labeled as push down & turn to open, but it was defective it opened with only a simple twist, without requiring downward pressure.

The product was being stored in my home and intended for supervised use by my children as a daily supplement. At the time of the incident, the bottle was in a secure location, but because the cap was not truly child-resistant, my children were able to open it.

I immediately contacted Poison Control for guidance, as I did not know what effects the gummies could have on my children. Fortunately, no serious injuries occurred in this case, but there was a clear risk of overdose or harm. If this had been another Garden of Life product, such as their childrens multivitamins containing higher-risk ingredients, the consequences could have been life-threatening.

This defective cap design presents a significant danger to children and fails to meet the safety expectations of child-resistant packaging.
justification: The incident involved children accessing and consuming a supplement due to a defective cap, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
The caller is reporting that her mother's Med-E-Lert Locking Automatic Pill dispenser from Group Medical Supply (GMS) is not working in a safe manner.  The clear cover that is supposed to dispense a single does of medicine sometimes overlaps the next dose section, which caused her 96 year old mother to overdose.  This occurred when the unit was turned over (as instructed) and shaken to release pills.  The caller's mother was not taken to the hospital but was cared for by the caller and the caller's husband, who is a physician. 

The caller tested the dispenser subsequently.  She said that when she turned the dispenser over and gave it a shake, pills from the next dose (particularly the small ones) could be released along with the expected dose.

She said the problem seems to be caused by some "play" in the rotation of the unit, so that rather than locking firmly into position, it can expose more than one dose, allowing additional pills to fall out when turned over.

This exact unit is also sold under the name "LiveFine", by a different distributer.  According to the Vice President of GMS, all the units are made by a single factory in China.

The caller has emailed photos of the dispenser to clearinghouse@cpsc.gov on 1/6/2017 with the appropriate report # in the subject line.  Also, photos attached to this report.
justification: The dispenser malfunction caused an overdose, but the patient was not hospitalized, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue was reproducible, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: My granddaughter received lacerations which also caused bleeding from the VERY sharp Ritz Crackers Handi Snacks package.
justification: The description mentions lacerations and bleeding, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer was unloading the packaging from a pick-up truck. The tailgate was down. 

The consumer was holding the packaging from a plastic handle in the back. There was a handle on the inner side and outer side of the box. Both of the handles gave away and separated from the cardboard box. This caused the consumer to lose her grip. It caused a shift in the box and the consumer crushed her left forearm in between the tail gate and the box. 

The consumer went to Urgent Care. There was a fracture in her Ulna on her left arm. The consumer was provided a soft brace by Urgent Care. The consumer was referred to an Orthopedic Surgeon. Few days later, the consumer saw an Orthopedic Surgeon. He put her in a half cast. 

On 12/23/15, the consumer was put in a soft brace again to allow some movement. They diagnosed that the fracture is not healing so the consumer has a surgery scheduled for 01/21/16 with the orthopedic surgeon.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer regarding the issue. The consumer spoke to the VP of Operations ([REDACTED]) at Emerald Home Furnishings. The consumer sent photos to [REDACTED]. The consumer was informed by him that he would send the photos and description of the incident to the insurance company. He contacted Alliance Global Corporate and Specialty and provided the adjusters information to the consumer.

The consumer contacted the adjuster directly after not hearing from anyone. The consumer spoke to [REDACTED] (Claims Adjuster II at Alliance Global Corporate and Specialty; Phone: 1-314-817-2967; Fax: 1-866-722-4317; Claim # [REDACTED]). She informed the consumer that she only received a copy of the receipt, description of the box and fuzzy picture from doctors report. The consumer sent all the files to her directly on 11/1/15. 

The consumer sent an e-mail to Ms. [REDACTED] after not receiving anything from her after the information was sent to her. The consumer also called her supervisor, [REDACTED], after not hearing from her. The consumer received an e-mail from Ms. [REDACTED] on 11/18/15 who informed her that she was trying to get more information on the box. 

On 12/8/15, the consumer contacted Ms.[REDACTED] informing her about the pending surgery and that she was still waiting on her case update. The consumer last contacted Ms. [REDACTED]  through e-mail on 1/12/16. As of 1/13/16, the consumer has not heard from Ms. [REDACTED]  on the status of her case. The consumer said that she has also tried to contact her through phone numerous times but no one calls her back after she leaves a message.

The consumer is not looking for compensation. She is looking to make sure that the company looks into the defect of the packaging so someone else does not suffer from a similar incident as her. 

The consumer stated that there were no warnings on the box that can inform the consumer to handle with care in case the handle breaks. 

(Treatment at Doctors Express Urgent Care)
justification: The incident resulted in a fracture requiring medical treatment and surgery, indicating an injury.

He was grabbing a tissue when he noticed a substance and he described it as dried vomit. He inspected the tissue box and he didn't notice signs of tampering from the outside. He indicated that he is a quarter into the box.

He plans to contact the firm and report the matter.

incident_description:
This was a manufacturing defect on the base of the twist off cap.
It was a standard 16.9 oz plastic bottle filled with Arrowhead Water (Nestle is the parent company).
When I opened the bottle by twisting the top of the cap, a sharp protrusion at the base of the plastic cap (that which remains on the bottle), sliced open my thumb about a half-inch.  I just opened it in the standard fashion - just twisting it as usual.  I usually drink bottled water on a regular basis - probably 5-6 bottles a day - for the past 30 years or so...not exclusively Arrowhead, and this is the third time in the past 5 years that I have had a similar occurrence, and all have been on Arrowhead bottles. It's the same small piece of protruding plastic that has cut me.  I still have the bottle and the sharp point, although small, is certainly large enough to cause the damage in each of the 3 injuries.
Now the cut to my left thumb was not severe, but t bleed for awhile, and I simply placed a bandage on it - I never required medical assistance on any of the 3 injuries.  I kept to bandaged for a week ( the pain was somewhat considerable, but the bandage controlled it.
I called up Arrowhead, and they told me that they could only offer me $5 for my pain and suffering...really both inadequate and insulting.   They gave me a case number:  [REDACTED]
Here's the thing:  I didn't report this to anyone because it wasn't a major injury (but it happened 3 times over about 5 years)...but it has no doubt happened to untold numbers of consumers over the years (with very few reporting it to you)..but it is a real problem, and I felt that I should be a good citizen and alert you folks as to what is should be considered a very painful, and moderately serious problem that has existed for a considerable period of time.  Hopefully, your department can do something about this product defect and the quality control associated with it.  Many thanks.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut thumb) that did not require medical attention, and the same issue has occurred multiple times over several years.

incident_description: Additional physical injuries sustained include:  lacerations to both upper and lower eyelids, severe swelling, headaches, and optic nerve damage; permanent blindness in his left eye. The adverse psychological effects are constant and ongoing, he was never depressed. Ever aspect of his life, daily routine activities, are now difficult for him.  previous to this catastrophic injury the same tasks were performed with great ease; without a second thought.The injury, along with losing his sight has significantly diminished his overall quality of life.  His left eye was his "good eye", his  dominate eye, as he could see well from it.No reasonable person would expect to be bloodied and blinded by their favorite beverage container. Yeti products have an inherently flawed design and pose a significant hazardous threat to be seriously injured or loss of life.
justification: The description details severe physical injuries including permanent blindness and significant psychological impact, indicating a high severity level. The likelihood is assessed as rare given the unexpected nature of the incident.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Product Safety Commission,

I am writing to formally report a serious safety issue with the Snapware Pyrex 18-piece Glass Food Storage Set, which poses a risk of injury due to glass chipping and contamination.

On July 7, while eating lunch stored in one of the round glass containers from this set, I bit into a piece of broken glass. Upon inspection, I found that the glass rim had chipped off, likely caused by pressure from the plastic lid snapping into place. Several other containers from the same set also show signs of similar chipping and damage along the rims.

This is not an isolated incident. I had previously noticed small shards of glass from this set but did not connect them to a design flaw until this more serious incident occurred. The potential for internal injury, especially to children or vulnerable adults, is significant.

I contacted the manufacturers customer service on July 8 and was told the issue would be escalated. However, I have received no response or resolution as of today (July 12). I also submitted an email complaint on July 9 with documentation and have not received any acknowledgment.

I believe this product presents a defect in either design or manufacturing and warrants immediate investigation. I am unable to attach photos in this message, but I would be happy to provide photographic evidence and a copy of my original complaint upon request.

Please let me know the best way to proceed or if you need any additional information to investigate this matter.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from ingesting glass, and multiple containers show similar damage indicating a likely recurring issue.
